bounded_slice.candidate: RFC 8949 deterministic CBOR as a reproducible byte-serialization profile for a fixed evidence package
bounded_slice.tested_scope: Static inspection of exactly one official RFC Editor primary source, RFC 8949. Tested only whether a fixed evidence package can be assigned a reproducible byte representation suitable as the input to later hashing/signing without an external execution handoff. No second public source, CBOR implementation execution, digest computation, signing, verification, external service, protected-primary action, manual-user execution, scheduler mutation, or other-worker/downstream/O semantic input was consumed.
observations: RFC 8949 section 4.2 explicitly defines restrictions that can serve as the base of a deterministic CBOR format.

Core deterministic encoding requires preferred serialization, so integer/length/tag arguments use the shortest allowed representation and floating-point values use the shortest representation preserving the value.
Core deterministic encoding forbids indefinite-length items.
Core deterministic encoding requires every map's keys to be sorted by bytewise lexicographic order of their deterministic encodings.

Section 4.2.2 warns that protocol-level choices can still defeat determinism unless the profile fixes them, including whether semantically optional tags are present and how numerically equivalent floating-point/integer forms, NaN, subnormals, or alternative tagged numeric forms are represented.
bounded_slice.inference: Positive for the narrow serialization-specification child: a fixed evidence-package profile can obtain reproducible CBOR bytes by requiring RFC 8949 core deterministic encoding and eliminating the remaining application-level representation choices. For this evidence package, the safe profile should use definite-length maps/arrays, deterministic map-key ordering, preferred serialization, and fixed field types; it should avoid optional tags and floating-point values unless their exact deterministic representation is separately specified. This establishes a byte-level deterministic serialization rule suitable for later hashing/signing, but does not establish that the current Chat surface can execute a conforming CBOR encoder.
bounded_slice.uncertainty: RFC 8949 defines a deterministic encoding framework, not a universal canonical byte sequence for every possible application data model. If the evidence schema permits semantically interchangeable tags, multiple numeric domains, NaN/subnormal variants, or other representation choices, extra profile rules are required. No implementation test was run, so actual scheduled-Chat CBOR encoding and byte-for-byte replay remain unresolved.
bounded_slice.replayability: A replaying implementation can regenerate the same CBOR byte representation for the fixed evidence package when both sides apply the same restricted evidence schema plus RFC 8949 core deterministic encoding rules; actual encoder availability/execution in scheduled Chat remains unresolved.
bounded_slice.hidden_executor_absence: The static standards inspection and serialization-profile binding required no external execution handoff. Concrete CBOR encoding, digest computation, COSE signing/verification, key trust, replay/freshness policy, PROV-to-JSON mapping, and observation/inference/uncertainty schema remain unresolved children and are not assumed.
